text:
Alice M.: quick async question — current API contract when both `pin` and routing hints (region/tier) are provided: which takes precedence? spotted ambiguous behavior in a client test.

Brian (eng-platform): ah yeah this comes up a lot. current intent in code is `pin` wins: if you pin to a model id we try to serve that exact model (and region only matters if the pinned model has regional availability). If pinned model not available in requested region we fall back per the model-variant fallback order, not by respecting the hint.

Carla - runtime: is that documented anywhere? iirc docs say hints are "preferences" but not strict. backward-compat worry: earlier clients relied on hints to route to cheaper tier even when pinning a family id (e.g., `redwood-3b`), so behavior change could break them.

Alice M.: here's a minimal example payload that tripped our test:
```json
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-3b@v2",
  "pin": "redwood-3b@v1",
  "routing_hints": { "region": "eu-west-1", "tier": "spot" },
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]
}
```
Alice M.: client expected to get v1 served in eu-west on spot nodes, but observed v2 served from us-west on on-demand.

Brian (eng-platform): that suggests runtime preferred the explicit `model` field over the `pin` field — are you sure payload isn't being normalized by the SDK? we treat `pin` as a pin to a model family/version and `model` is the requested model id; historically `pin` was a server-side override to keep an allocation, but there are two meanings in older clients.

Carla - runtime: I checked the selection code: the selection priority is (1) explicit `model` param, (2) pinned assignment for the customer, (3) routing hints. So if you specify both `model` and `pin` in request body that's ambiguous; we should reject that. Right now we fallback to `model` which explains this.

SRE Oncall: fwiw, for Dedicated customers we auto-honor `pin` as a hard affinity to reserved pools. For Hosted, pins are weaker unless customer has a reserved mapping. This inconsistency is bad.

Brian (eng-platform): consensus proposal: server should validate and enforce a clear precedence and/or return 400 when client supplies conflicting selectors. options:
- reject requests that include both `model` and `pin` (safer, breaking but explicit)
- accept both but define deterministic precedence (`model` wins, pin is advisory)
- accept both and interpret `pin` as "pin the family if `model` absent" (current-ish), plus surface warning header `X-Pin-Ignored: true`

Alice M.: i'd prefer a 400 with helpful error for first pass (forces clients to be explicit). we can then add a migration window and logs.

Carla - runtime: agree on 400 for hosted API. For Dedicated customers we need a separate rule (pin -> reserved capacity) so behavior config should be per-customer. I'll sketch an ACL check.

Brian (eng-platform): also need to clarify how `routing_hints` interact with fallback orders. propose rule: hints are soft preferences that only apply after the primary selector (model/pin) can't be served in the requested location. e.g., flow: compute candidate set from selector -> filter by region/tier hint if possible -> if empty, run fallback policy. This keeps hints non-breaking.

Alice M.: ok. small doc patch needed for API and for runtime selection logic. also add a conformance test: send conflicting payloads and assert 400, send pin-only payload and assert `served_model` in response equals pinned model or a clear fallback with `served_model` and `served_variant` fields.

Brian (eng-platform): agreed. i'll add a lint rule to the request validator: if both `model` and `pin` present -> 400 + error code `conflicting_selectors`. i'll open PR for validator.

Carla - runtime: i'll add unit tests in runtime repo and a runtime config flag `honor_pin_for_dedicated` (default true for dedicated, false for hosted). also i'll add a metric `pin_ignored` to help monitor.

Alice M.: will someone take the docs PR? i can draft but bandwidth low this week. @Brian could you stub the API doc changes so we have wording?

Brian (eng-platform): yeah i can add a stub and link to the design doc. i'll also include example responses: success case includes `served_model` and `served_region` fields and a `warnings` array if hints ignored. example: 
```json
{ "id": "abc", "served_model": "redwood-3b@v1", "served_region": "eu-west-1", "warnings": ["routing_hint:tier ignored: not available in eu-west-1"] }
```

Deploy Bot: CI build for runtime tests passed: https://ci.internal/builds/5123 :white_check_mark:

SRE Oncall: one operational note — we should ensure rollback policy if honoring pin to a single region causes capacity pressure in that region. maybe auto-fallback to next region and surface `degradation` event.

Carla - runtime: noted. i'll add a canary policy and an event emission `route_degraded` when we fall back region/tier.

Alice M.: action items: (1) Brian -> validator PR (conflicting_selectors 400) (2) Carla -> runtime flag + tests + metric + event (3) Brian -> docs stub + example responses (4) Alice -> compatibility note + test matrix in evals repo. i'll open tickets.

Brian (eng-platform): thanks — i'll ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:

Carla - runtime: thanks all, will follow up with exact metric names.

Alice M.: thanks — landing this will make routing behavior much easier to reason about for customers. :rocket:
